messages:
maya: Heads-up — while spinning up the new inference fleet in ap-southeast-1 we hit a hard failure registering targets on the NLB. Provisioning stalled at ~48/50 targets and then started 500s. Anyone else seen this today?

devon: yup saw a couple failed rolling deploys. error looked like "Target registration limit exceeded" from the ELB API.

maya: exact error from the node agent: `ValidationError: Maximum number of targets per target group exceeded`. We're trying to add 120 GPU nodes across 3 target groups (spread for AZs).

raj: do we need to increase "Targets per target group" or split into more TGs? What's the account limit for NLB targets in ap-southeast-1?

maya: looks like default is 50 targets per target group. Our plan assumed 100+ per TG for single-service routing to avoid cross-TG sticky routing. Splitting would complicate health checks and routing.

devon: cost tradeoff too — more TGs = more target registration churn and more LB rules to manage. Would prefer quota bump if possible.

maya: I started a console support ticket and drafted an AWS quota increase request. Here's the ask I put in the ticket: 
```
Service: Elastic Load Balancing (ELB)
Quota: Targets per target group
Region: ap-southeast-1
Current: 50
Requested: 500
Account: 123456789012
Reason: Production inference fleet expansion for Redwood Dedicated; need capacity for 120+ GPU nodes per service to maintain AZ-balanced throughput and failover.
```

infra-bot: Ticket #AWS-104712 created: "Request quota increase for Targets per target group in ap-southeast-1" — status: Open. (link: https://console.aws.amazon.com/support/home#/case/?caseId=AWS-104712)

raj: also double-check VPC ENI limits and ENIs-per-instance for our GPU instance types — NLB target registration can fail if ENI limits hit during scale-up. Which instance family are these?

maya: G5x family (g5.2xlarge & g5.12xlarge mix). We should be fine on ENIs per instance, but I'll run the math.

devon: another limit to keep an eye on: Interface endpoints per VPC and private endpoint quotas — our private endpoints for control plane + model store could also be hitting quotas as we provision in new AZs.

maya: good call. I added an extra note in the support case asking them to verify there are no account-level blocks for NLB target registrations and to confirm per-region soft limits for ELB.

cloud-support: AWS support responded: "We can increase Targets per target group to 500 for account 123456789012 in ap-southeast-1. Pending internal review — ETA 48–72 hours. Please confirm you have validated ENI, IP address, and route table limits."

raj: nice. I'll cross-check ENI and subnet IP exhaustion in the prod VPCs. If any subnets are tight we should expand or add secondary CIDR before the scaling window.

maya: thanks — I'll hold the fleet rollout until we get confirmation. If support approves, we can resume this afternoon's rolling deploy. :pray:

devon: if AWS is slow, fallback plan: split the service into 4 TGs and add an internal ALB in front for sticky routing during the window. Ugly but doable.

maya: noted. I'll also add a quick runbook step to the deploy checklist: "Verify NLB target quota >= desired nodes" and include the support case link.

infra-bot: Reminder: create follow-up ticket to track cost impact of requested quota bump (more TG scale testing) and update the SRE playbook if we change architecture.

maya: added a TODO in the infra board. Will post updates when support moves the case. :eyes:
